extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent applicants, patent office officials, and legal professionals working on U.S. patents
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted statutory and judicial standards governing U.S. patent practice (office procedures, applicant requirements, remedies, fees, and judicial interpretations of patentability) as reflected in the cited Acts and Judge Cranch's decisions. Useful for practitioners assessing compliance, enforceability, and patentability under 19th-century U.S. law principles reflected here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial validity for bona fide claimed parts; disclaimer requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: So much of the invention or discovery as shall be truly and bona fide his own ... shall be deemed good and valid for so much of the invention or discovery as shall be truly and bona fide his own: Provided, It shall be a material and substantial part of the thing patented, and be definitively distinguishable from the other parts so claimed without right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a specification embraces more than the applicant has a right to claim, the patent is valid for the material/substantial portion that is bona fide the patentee's. The patentee may sue for infringement of that part, but to recover costs he must have entered at the Patent Office, prior to suit commencement, a disclaimer of the part claimed without right. Unreasonable delay or neglect in entering the disclaimer may forfeit benefits of these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents authorized to receive models and specimens in principal cities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner is authorized to appoint agents, not exceeding twenty, in principal cities or towns to receive and forward to the Patent Office models, specimens of ingredients, and manufactures intended to be patented or deposited therein, transportation chargeable to the patent fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure for decentralized receipt of physical deposit material; costs borne by patent fund. Relevant for applicants needing to deposit models/specimens outside Washington.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and compensation of examining, copying, and temporary clerks
rubrics_metrics.description: Two examining clerks and an additional copying clerk are to be appointed with specified annual salaries; Commissioner may employ temporary clerks as necessary and pay copying clerks per page rates and reasonable compensation for drawings and record comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative staffing and compensation rules: permanent salaries stated; temporary clerks may be hired and paid per-page rates (e.g., seven cents per 100-word page for copying) or such compensation as Commissioner prescribes. Affects office throughput and fee-funded expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund to foreign applicants upon rejection for want of novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the application of any foreigner for a patent shall be rejected and withdrawn for want of novelty ... the certificate thereof of the Commissioner shall be a sufficient warrant to the Treasurer to pay back to such applicant two-thirds of the duty he shall have paid into the Treasury on account of such application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejected for lack of novelty, foreign applicants may recover two-thirds of the duty paid, upon Commissioner's certificate—procedural refund mechanism for certain rejected foreign applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmation may substitute for oath when conscientiously scrupulous
rubrics_metrics.description: In all cases in which an oath is required by this act ... if the person of whom it is required shall be conscientiously scrupulous of taking an oath, affirmation may be substituted therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief for applicants or witnesses refusing religious oaths; affirmation has identical legal effect where authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent fund accounting and annual reporting duties of Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: All moneys paid into the Treasury for patents and for fees ... shall be carried to the credit of the patent fund and appropriated for Patent Office salaries and expenses. The Commissioner shall lay before Congress annually a detailed statement of expenditures and a list of patents granted and patents become public property, with other useful information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial governance: patent fees fund office operation and must be reported to Congress yearly, including an annual patent list and patent-holder directory.

rubrics_metrics.name: No debarment for prior foreign patent if not introduced into U.S. public use; term limited to 14 years
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall be debarred from receiving a patent by reason of the same having been patented in a foreign country more than six months prior to his application: Provided, That the same shall not have been introduced into public and common use in the United States prior to the application; and every such patent shall be limited to the term of fourteen years from the date of publication of such foreign letters-patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign patenting within six months before a U.S. application does not automatically bar U.S. patenting unless the invention was introduced into public use in the U.S. Patent term in such cases is limited to 14 years measured from the foreign patent publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior purchasers' rights and exceptions to invalidity based on prior purchase/use
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who have purchased or constructed any newly invented machine, manufacture, or composition of matter prior to the inventor's application shall have the right to use and vend that specific machine ... without liability to the inventor; and no patent shall be invalid by reason of such purchase, sale, or use except on proof of abandonment or that such purchase, sale, or prior use has been for more than two years prior to application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes prior user/purchaser rights and limits on invalidating patents due to prior commercial activity—requires proof of abandonment or long prior commercial use (>2 years) to invalidate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording assignments and conveyances: fee rules (repeal then later fee schedule)
rubrics_metrics.description: At one point assignments, grants, and conveyances were to be recorded without any charge whatever (repeal of $3 fee). Later authority (1848) required a fee of $1 for instruments not exceeding 300 words, $2 for >300 up to 1,000 words, and $3 for over 1,000 words, payable in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording cost regime changed over time: practitioners must comply with the applicable fee schedule in effect at filing time; failure to pay may affect recordation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Chief Justice: notice, written reasons, $25 fee, scope confined to reasons of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appeal is allowed from the Commissioner, the party may appeal to the Chief Justice of the District of Columbia by giving notice, filing in the Patent Office within the prescribed time his reasons of appeal specifically set forth in writing, and paying $25 into the patent fund. The Chief Justice shall hear and determine such appeals and revise decisions in a summary way on the evidence produced before the Commissioner, confined to the points involved by the reasons of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal procedure specifics: limited scope of review (confined to the written reasons and Commissioner's grounds), summary disposition, requirement that Commissioner lay before the judge the originals and grounds, and fees to be paid. Commissioner and examiners may be examined under oath; judge returns papers with certificate, but decision does not preclude later judicial contest in other courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner power to prescribe regulations for taking evidence in contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of Patents shall have power to make all such regulations in respect to the taking of evidence to be used in contested cases before him, as may be just and reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation of evidentiary rule-making authority to the Commissioner—affects evidentiary practices in office contests and appeals to the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for false marking or imitation of patentee's stamp or device
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person shall affix the word 'patent' or 'letters-patent' or 'patentee' or any imitation thereof on any thing made, used, or sold for which he has not letters-patent, or affix such words on any unpatented article for the purpose of deceiving the public, he shall be liable to a penalty of not less than one hundred dollars, with costs, to be recovered by action in U.S. circuit or district courts; one-half to the patent fund and the other half to the person who shall sue for the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict deterrent against false patent marking and counterfeiting patentee's marks; private enforcement incentivized through half-the-penalty award to successful private plaintiff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to mark articles with date of patent; penalty for neglect
rubrics_metrics.description: All patentees and assignees of patents are required to stamp or engrave on each article vended or offered for sale the date of the patent; neglect to do so renders them liable to the same penalty and disposition specified for false marking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes affirmative marking duty on patent holders; failure subjects patentees/assignees to monetary penalties similar to false marking penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner vested with exclusive power to extend patents; extension limited and procedure set
rubrics_metrics.description: Power to extend patents, formerly vested in a board (Secretary of State, Commissioner, Solicitor), is vested solely in the Commissioner; when application is made for extension and sixty days' notice given, the Commissioner shall refer the case to the principal examiner of the class, who shall report whether the invention or improvement was new and patentable when patented; no extension shall be for longer than seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure for extension: referral to principal examiner for factual/patentability determination as of original patent date; Commissioner decides on the same principles that governed the former board; statutory maximum extension = 7 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treasurer may repay mistakenly paid patent fees upon Commissioner's certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treasurer is authorized to pay back out of the patent fund any sum or sums of money which shall have been paid into the Treasury as for fees accruing at the Patent Office through mistake, certificate thereof being made to the Treasurer by the Commissioner of Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refund mechanism for mistaken payments, requiring Commissioner's certification to Treasurer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal of lost patents (extension of prior-act renewal provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The act authorizing renewing of patents lost prior to a given date was extended to patents granted prior to that date though subsequently lost, provided they had not been recorded anew under the act's provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative remedy for lost patent documents under specified temporal conditions—practitioners should ensure compliance with recordation requirements to use renewal remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oaths by applicants abroad may be taken before U.S. ministers/consuls or notaries
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath required for applicants for patents when the applicant is not residing in the United States may be taken before any minister, plenipotentiary, chargé d'affaires, consul, or commercial agent holding commission under the U.S. government, or before any notary public of the foreign country where the applicant is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates nonresident applicants' compliance with oath requirements using U.S. diplomatic or consular officers or local notaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designs, patterns, sculptures etc. may receive a seven-year patent with half fees for certain applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Any citizen or alien having resided one year in the United States and taken the oath of intention to become a citizen, who has by his own industry produced any new and original design for a manufacture, printing, sculpture, ornament, impression, shape, or configuration not known or used by others before, may apply for exclusive property by petition; fee in such cases shall be one-half the usual sum and duration of said patent shall be seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a category akin to design patents (new and original designs/ornaments/shapes) with a reduced fee and a seven-year exclusivity term; other patent regulations apply unless inconsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on patenting mere discovery of beneficial effect of preexisting acts or arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention, if it be one, must consist in producing something that did not exist before; the discovery of a beneficial effect of an arrangement or act which existed before (e.g., placing ice blocks edgewise) is not a new thing and thus not the subject of a patent. Discovery differs from invention: discovery brings to light what existed before, invention produces something that did not before exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial interpretation (Judge Cranch): an applicant cannot secure a patent for merely discovering that a previously-known practice has a beneficial effect. The patent system secures inventors for contriving or producing new things, not for post-hoc discoveries about preexisting matters. Examine whether the claimed subject matter is an act/arrangement previously done; if so, patentability is doubtful even if the beneficial effect was newly observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must be the inventor and provide a written description distinguishing the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must invent, contrive, or produce something that did not exist before; statutes require the applicant to swear or affirm that he is the true inventor or discoverer and to deliver a written description of his invention by which it may be distinguished from other inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional/ statutory requirement that patents be granted to the inventor. Specifications must include a written description adequate to distinguish the claimed invention from prior art/other inventions—used to determine entitlement and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject matter: must be a new and useful art or improvement not before known or used
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are for a new and useful art, manufacture, or improvement therein, not before known or used; the discovery of a new art that will justify a patent can only be the invention of a new art, and the discovery of a new improvement the invention of a new improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core novelty and utility requirement: to be patentable the subject must represent a new and useful art or improvement not previously known or used. Courts read statutory 'discovery' in the sense of 'invention' for patentability analysis—focus on novelty over mere discovery of effects.
